Here is how we can list the models that contain data for variables pr, rsds using intake-esgf in python:
```python
from intake_esgf import ESGFCatalog

# initialize the catalog
cat = ESGFCatalog()

# specify variables to search for
variables = ["pr", "rsds"]

# search the catalog for models with the specified variable
search_results = cat.search(
    variable_id=variables
)

# get a list of unique models
models = sorted(search_results.df["source_id"].unique())

# print out our results
print(f"Models({len(models)} results):")
for i, model in enumerate(models):
    print(f"{i+1}. {model}")
```

frequency = ["1hr"]

    frequency=frequency
)

```python
from intake_esgf import ESGFCatalog

# initialize the catalog
cat = ESGFCatalog()

# specify variables to search for
variables = ["tos", "evspsbl"]
frequency = ["dec"]

# search the catalog for models with the specified variable
search_results = cat.search(
    variable_id=variables
    frequency=frequency
)

# get a list of unique models
models = sorted(search_results.df["source_id"].unique())

# print out our results
print(f"Models({len(models)} results):")
for i, model in enumerate(models):
    print(f"{i+1}. {model}")
```

    frequency=frequency
)

```python
from intake_esgf import ESGFCatalog

# initialize the catalog
cat = ESGFCatalog()

# specify variables to search for
variables = ["gpp", "rsds", "evspsbl"]
frequency = ["fx"]

# search the catalog for models with the specified variable
search_results = cat.search(
    variable_id=variables
    frequency=frequency
)

# get a list of unique models
models = sorted(search_results.df["source_id"].unique())

# print out our results
print(f"Models({len(models)} results):")
for i, model in enumerate(models):
    print(f"{i+1}. {model}")
```

```python
from intake_esgf import ESGFCatalog

# initialize the catalog
cat = ESGFCatalog()

# specify variables to search for
variables = ["rsds", "tas"]
frequency = ["mon"]

# search the catalog for models with the specified variable
search_results = cat.search(
    variable_id=variables
    frequency=frequency
)

# get a list of unique models
models = sorted(search_results.df["source_id"].unique())

# print out our results
print(f"Models({len(models)} results):")
for i, model in enumerate(models):
    print(f"{i+1}. {model}")
```
